text:
lian: quick heads-up. multiple Expo/React Native users reporting that the JS SDK crashes the packager or runtime because Metro pulls the wrong entry (ESM/node-targeted) and RN lacks node builtins like crypto/stream. anyone reproduced?

ben: reproduced with a small repro. Metro 0.66/0.72 behave differently. Metro ignores conditional exports in some versions, ends up loading our ESM edge bundle which calls ReadableStream and imports 'node:crypto'. error seen in expo: 

Invariant Violation: Can't find module: stream
TypeError: undefined is not a function (evaluating 'new ReadableStream(...)')

jess: expo-managed users hit this a lot. They don't have Buffer, crypto, or node stream. Typical band-aid is to install react-native-get-random-values + react-native-crypto shim, but that's rough UX and breaks fast refresh sometimes.

alice: options: 1) publish a dedicated react-native entry (dist/rn/index.js) and reference it via package.json "react-native" field and exports; 2) ship a tiny RN shim bundle that polyfills crypto.getRandomValues, TextEncoder, and a minimal fetch-based streaming fallback; 3) update docs and sample app.

ben: proposed package.json snippet that should make Metro pick the RN build:

{"main":"dist/cjs/index.js","module":"dist/esm/index.js","react-native":"dist/rn/index.js","exports":{".":{"import":"dist/esm/index.js","require":"dist/cjs/index.js","react-native":"dist/rn/index.js"}},"types":"dist/types/index.d.ts"}

jess: +1. Metro respects react-native field. dist/rn/index.js can re-export the public API but import RN-friendly internals (no node:crypto, no ReadableStream).

lian: minimal rn-shims we can include (or point to in README):

// rn-shims.js
import 'react-native-get-random-values'; // fills globalThis.crypto.getRandomValues
if (!globalThis.crypto) globalThis.crypto = { getRandomValues: globalThis.getRandomValues };
if (!globalThis.TextEncoder) globalThis.TextEncoder = class { encode(s){ return new Uint8Array([...Buffer.from(String(s), 'utf8')]); } };
// fallback for streaming-only APIs: small helper that converts fetch() responses to simple async iterator
if (!globalThis.ReadableStream) {
  globalThis.ReadableStream = class { constructor(){ throw new Error('ReadableStream not available in RN. Use response.text() or the RN shim helpers.'); } };
}

ben: also watch types: avoid referencing @types/node in the RN build declarations. If our d.ts pulls in NodeJS.ReadableStream, TS projects bring in @types/node which causes conflicts. Ensure dist/types references browser-safe types and the rn index.d.ts is a copy or wrapper without node typings.

alice: docs: update README to clearly call out supported runtimes per bundle: node (server), edge (streaming-first ESM), browser, react-native/expo (rn bundle + shims). People were using the top-level ESM import example for RN which led to runtime failures.

jess: CI suggestion: add an Expo minimal sample app under examples/expo-minimal and a CI job that runs `expo prebuild` + `metro` bundle step to catch bundling issues across metro versions. We don't need an emulator; just ensure bundling succeeds. matrix: expo-managed latest SDK, bare RN 0.69+, metro 0.66/0.72/0.74.

ben: ACTIONS:
- ben: PR to add dist/rn bundle, rn-shims, and package.json exports. target EOD Thu.
- jess: add examples/expo-minimal and README notes for shims + expo-managed quickstart.
- alice: docs PR clarifying runtime bundles and typing guidance (avoid @types/node in RN).

ci-bot: CI run started for branch sdk/rn-compat (https://ci.internal/runs/12345) :gear:

jess: testing local quickfix now (import 'react-native-get-random-values' + globalThis.crypto shim) will report back if bundling still fails.

lian: thanks. if you hit more errors paste the full metro error + expo/sdk + metro versions. :thumbsup:
